author: 5kO0
content:
Implemented (this session). Added two new differential tests covering audit items 1+2 (dag-cbor encode parity, CID derivation parity) — items 3-5 (MST shape, CAR layout, commit construction) are stackable extensions filed as follow-ups.

Wire format design: tagged-enum JSON (NOT lex-json) so the parity check isn't coupled to the lex-json codec's own correctness. Both sides build a native IPLD value from the wire format and feed it to their respective dag-cbor encoders.

Files added/changed:
  proto-blue-interop-tests/Cargo.toml         — added proto-blue-lex-cbor dep
  proto-blue-interop-tests/ts-runner/package.json — added @atproto/common 0.4.12 + multiformats 13.4.0
  proto-blue-interop-tests/ts-runner/index.mjs    — async dispatch + 2 new ops:
                                                     - cbor_encode_lexvalue: LexValueJson → {hex}
                                                     - cid_for_lexvalue: LexValueJson → {cid}
                                                     plus lexValueJsonToIpld() builder with strict shape-checking
  proto-blue-interop-tests/tests/differential.rs  — lex_value_to_wire(), 28-fixture cbor_parity_corpus(),
                                                     differential_dag_cbor_encode + differential_cid_for_lexvalue

Adversarial corpus (28 fixtures) covers:
  - Scalars: null, true, false, 0, 1, -1
  - CBOR major-type-0/1 length-encoding boundaries: 23, 24, 255, 256, 65535, u32::MAX
  - JS-safe integer extremes: ±(2^53 - 1)
  - Strings: empty, ASCII, multi-byte UTF-8 (with emoji)
  - Bytes: empty, 4-byte, 300-byte (crosses CBOR len thresholds)
  - CID values
  - Empty array, empty map
  - Map with sort-edge keys (same-length lexicographic tiebreaks, varied-length shorter-first, multi-byte UTF-8 keys)
  - Nested map (map containing array + map)
  - 3-deep nested array

Found one real divergence during fixture-tuning: i64::MAX produced different bytes (1b7fffffffffffffff vs fb43e0000000000000) — TS lost precision because i64::MAX is beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so it became an f64 in JSON transit. NOT a codec bug; a JSON wire-format limitation. Capped corpus integers at JS-safe range (±(2^53-1)) and documented the limitation. The Rust-only integer-encoding tests in proto-blue-lex-cbor still cover i64::MIN/MAX.

Items 3-5 (MST / CAR / commit construction) intentionally NOT in this delivery — each is a substantial extension with its own fixture-design conversation (random key/cid set generation, block-sequence ordering, keypair fixtures + signing-payload determinism). Spinning out as separable follow-ups (#26, #27, #28 below).

Verification (rust-quality §honest reporting):
  cargo build -p proto-blue-interop-tests --tests                   PASS
  cargo build --workspace                                           PASS
  cargo test --workspace                                            PASS (67 suites, 0 failures — new tests skip cleanly without TS_RUNNER_READY)
  cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings             PASS
  cargo fmt --all --check                                           PASS
  Live: TS_RUNNER_READY=1 cargo test -p proto-blue-interop-tests differential_dag_cbor: PASS — 28-fixture parity holds byte-exact against @atproto/common::cborEncode
  Live: TS_RUNNER_READY=1 cargo test -p proto-blue-interop-tests differential_cid:      PASS — 28-fixture CID derivation matches @atproto/common::cidForCbor

Behavioural change: none in production code. New tests are TS_RUNNER_READY-gated (skip silently in default cargo test) so the per-PR build stays network-free. The interop CI job runs them by setting the env var.

Category: A (root-cause) — added the missing cross-impl validation pathway end-to-end (TS adapter ops, Rust corpus, parity assertions, deps wired). The audit's primary value at the codec boundary is now realised: any future regression in dag-cbor map-sort, integer-encoding, CID-tag-42 framing, or sha256-multibase-CID derivation will surface in CI as a byte-mismatch, not as silent behavioural drift.

The audit-comment review by the jacquard author is now fully addressed end-to-end:
  Audit items   Status
  ────────────  ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  proof tests   #2 closed (property + fuzz)
  String->newtypes  #3 + #6 + #21 closed (codegen, Agent surface, XRPC params)
  codegen lints     #5 + #23 + #24 + #25 closed (edition-2024 keywords, leaf-and-parent, dash segments, multi-line descriptions)
  unions            #4 closed (synthetic sum types)
  Cid heap-alloc    #7 closed ([u8; 32])
  serde_ipld_dagcbor #8 closed via reassessment (LexValue lacks serde impl; would add net code)
  float strictness  #9 closed (decode_lenient no longer coerces integral floats)
  interop diff      #10 closed (this) — items 1+2 done, 3-5 spun out

Suggested next: pick up the #26/#27/#28 follow-ups if interop coverage of MST/CAR/commit is wanted, OR ship a release pulling in the audit-driven changes.
